I started playing Hollow Knight just over a year ago, and yet I still remember that first playthrough like it was yesterday. Before Hollow Knight I was like a sheltered toddler in terms of what kind of games I played. A lot of Nintendo. Some Minecraft. A few indie games. So when I booted up Hollow Knight for the first time, I had absolutely no idea what to expect.

The first couple hours were rough. Really, really rough. I was convinced I had finally bought a game that I simply wasn't going to enjoy. The enemies were ridiculously punishing, I had absolutely no sense of direction, and there wasn't even a clear objective of where to go next.

Then, slowly, but surely, I start to get my bearings. 3 hours later, time seems to disappear and I become fully immersed in the beauty of Hallownest. Every inch of the map was something new; the game never punished you for exploring every nook and cranny. It was so rewarding, and the more I played the more I understood just how expansive the world was.

Fast forward 217 hours, and I had every achievement and had 112% completed the game four separate times, including on Steel Soul. And I loved every second of it. This game is not one to sleep on.

The soundtrack is [i]immaculate[/i]. Often times you don't even notice it and it blends in perfectly with the environment. Other times it perfectly captures the scale of a cutscene, like Sealed Vessel.

The art direction is also phenomenal. Every little detail is accounted for, and every area has something unique about it. There are few things more rewarding than sitting down at the hidden bench in Greenpath, with a beautiful waterfall in the background to accompany you. Or walking into City of Tears for the first time. Or brutally navigating your way through Deepnest on one singular mask and finding relief at an unexpected hot spring.

The progression is done incredibly well. I would by no means describe Hollow Knight as linear, yet you can still always tell when you've made progress. The game also handles difficulty really well. Most players agree that the early game of Hollow Knight [i]feels[/i] the hardest, even though the late and end game are objectively harder. This is because by the time you make it to those sections, they don't feel unfair, as the game has already taught you how to overcome them.

I'm writing this review for my 1 year anniversary since I started playing to reminisce on what a masterpiece this game is. If you're somehow lucky enough to have never played it, PLEASE do. You will not regret it and will enjoy this game for a very long time.

很久以前买的，用键盘玩到真菌荒地，被下劈弹跳搞崩了，就一直扔在库中。
今年尝试了下手柄，完美解决下劈问题，于是一路玩了起来。这次重玩游戏评论分别在10小时，40小时，和现在60小时通关写了第三次。
10小时的时候因为下劈困扰解决，很长一段时间没有遇到什么搞心态的内容，觉得终于尝到了这个游戏的乐趣，写了一段推荐好评。
40多小时的时候，因为在白宫和无尽的跑地图中感到很枯燥，加上游戏中各种小恶意的设计积累到一起，把推荐改成了不推荐，并写了一堆差评。
现在通关了，心态已经不那么不爽了，平心而论是个好游戏，只是我对这种游戏真的无感。而且通关后，依然不推荐没接触过类似游戏的玩家入坑，游戏难是一方面，它很多难度是体现在让玩家别扭的地方。
这类游戏本身因为2D的限制，可以发挥的空间比较小，所以制作团队在难度提升上只能选择为难玩家的途径去增加游戏时间。喜欢跳跳乐的玩家不容错过。
游戏的剧情碎片魂式，可能很多人喜欢去挖掘解读，但是就这作本身来说，没有太多深度的细节可以挖，毕竟是个小型游戏。
游戏音乐初听很好听，但是整个游戏玩下来，本身剧情就比较阴暗晦涩，游戏BGM也很阴郁，所以整个游戏玩起来会很沉重的感觉，后期我都是把音乐关了。
全篇最喜欢的boss是梦魇格林，有清晰的攻击逻辑，节奏也非常紧凑，相反辐光是我最不喜欢的boss，就是变种跳跳乐。神居我开了一个boss都没打，这作所有的boss攻击基本就几个技能，通过不停重复，随机抽卡技能来体现难度，游戏本身机制限制没办法，所以基本就是在考验熟练度和跳跳把握。
跳完100%进度，游戏就删了。丝之歌不打算尝试。
